title: Apple Catch
body:
Goal: build a catch game with a score variable, random start places, a forever loop and if blocks. Tool: Scratch app (offline). Work in pairs: swap, then play each other's game.

Build steps

  1. Start a new project. Delete the cat. Add the Bowl and Apple sprites (Choose a Sprite). Choose any backdrop.
  2. Make a variable score (For all sprites).
  3. Click the Bowl and build the Bowl script. mouse x is in Sensing.
  4. Click the Apple and build the Apple script. y position is in Motion; the < block is in Operators.
  5. Play: move the mouse left and right to catch the apples.
  6. Bug hunt: take the go to x: (pick random ...) y: 170 block out of the touching Bowl? block. Catch one apple. What happens to the score? Why? Put the block back.
  7. Add a credits comment and save as apple-catch.

The scripts in words

Bowl:

  • when green flag clicked
  • go to x: 0 y: -140
  • forever:
    • set x to (mouse x)

Apple:

  • when green flag clicked
  • set score to 0
  • go to x: (pick random -200 to 200) y: 170
  • forever:
    • change y by -5
    • if touching Bowl? then
      • change score by 1
      • start sound (any)
      • go to x: (pick random -200 to 200) y: 170
    • if (y position) < -170 then
      • go to x: (pick random -200 to 200) y: 170

Expected behavior

The score starts at 0. The bowl stays at the bottom and follows the mouse left and right. Apples fall from a different place at the top each time. Each apple you catch adds exactly 1 to the score and plays a sound; then a new apple falls. A missed apple starts again at the top. Without the "go to the top" block after a catch, one catch adds lots of points, because the apple keeps touching the bowl while the loop keeps checking.

Checklist

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the Bowl script and the Apple script separately. The Bowl only follows the mouse. The Apple does the falling, the counting, and the restarting.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Inside the Apple's forever loop, use two if blocks from the Control category. One asks if the apple touches the bowl (Sensing category). The other asks if the apple's y position (Motion category) is less than a low number (Operators category).

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Use change y by with a negative number so the apple falls. In the catch if, put change score by ____, then a sound, then a go to x: ____ y: ____ block. For the bug hunt, think about what the apple is doing right after you catch it.
